_note: Idioms and paraphrases for concepts with no single inherited word (docs/audits/lexicon-gaps-*.md). scripts/lexq.py prints every entry whose `english` list matches a query. `ids` are words a Tier 3 planner may use (never a coinage); `tier3b_ids` are coinages, shown only with --tier3b. `kind`: idiom (an inherited way of saying it, with daughter evidence), or paraphrase (no PIE word or idiom is defensible; `how` says what to write instead and `source` why). Forms and glosses only; no book text is quoted.

idioms.idiom: próti mléwHti 'speak back'
idioms.how: próti as an ADV slot just before the verb mléwHti; the engine has no preverb compounds
idioms.source: EWAia s.v. práti (Ved. práti-brav-, OAv. paiti.mrauu 'answer'); round 1 (lexicon-gaps-core-2026-10-30.md)

idioms.idiom: h₂epó Hwért 'turn (the door) away'
idioms.how: h₂epó as an ADV slot before Hwért (aorist only): 'he opened the door' = dʰwórom h₂epó Hwért
idioms.source: LIV² *Hu̯er- (Ved. ápa vṛ, Lat. aperiō < *ap-wer-, OCS ot-voriti); round 1

idioms.idiom: h₂éyeri 'early, in the morning' or h₂ewsér 'at dawn'
idioms.how: an ADV slot with a future-minded verb (subjunctive or present): 'tomorrow we go' = h₂éyeri h₁ímos
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §18.6: no PIE 'tomorrow'; Gk αὔριον is from 'at dawn' (Beekes); round 1

idioms.idiom: 'on this day': the near deictic + dínos in the locative
idioms.how: dínos in a LOC slot with closed:deictic_ki as its MOD
idioms.source: each branch builds 'this day' from its own demonstrative and day word (Lat. hodiē, Gk σήμερον, Skt adyá); round 1

idioms.idiom: praise the giver (gʷr̥néHti), call the gift welcome (gʷr̥Htós)
idioms.how: 'thank you' = 'I praise you' (gʷr̥néHti, 1SG, OBJ 'you'); 'grateful' = gʷr̥Htós
idioms.source: de Vaan 2008 s.v. grātus (*gʷr̥H-to-: Skt gūrtá- 'welcome', Lat. grātus); round 1

idioms.idiom: yes = repeat the question's verb; no = ne + the same verb
idioms.how: 'Did you see the wolf? Yes.' = an answer clause with the same verb lexeme (planner brief rule 13); 'No.' = the same clause with neg: "ne". Never invent a 'yes' word
idioms.source: no PIE word for 'yes' or 'no' reconstructs (none in M&A 2006 or Fortson 2010); planner brief rule 13 already has answers repeat the verb (round 3)

idioms.idiom: a subordinate clause with the particle h₁yód
idioms.how: "particle": "yod" on the reason clause (verb-final); put it before or after the main clause
idioms.source: Fortson 2010 §7.27: PIE subordinating conjunctions are case forms of pronouns (neut. acc. Hitt. kuit, Lat. quod 'because'); the engine's subordinator is h₁yód (Ved. yád)

idioms.idiom: the accusative of extent: the time noun in the accusative, no adposition
idioms.how: put the time noun in a GOAL slot (the role that gives ACC) with a numeral MOD: 'he slept three nights' = tísrn̥s nókʷtn̥s + verb. Count in nights where the text allows (Gaulish and Germanic reckoning)
idioms.source: Handbook (Klein, Joseph and Fritz 2017) ch. V Indic syntax: accusative of time; ch. VII Greek syntax: the accusative expresses duration in time or space

idioms.idiom: no PIE 'ago'
idioms.how: use dʰǵʰyés 'yesterday', péruti 'last year', or a past verb with an accusative of extent ('three nights we have walked')
idioms.source: no 'ago' construction reconstructs (round 3)

idioms.idiom: drive off the cattle: h₂éǵeti + gʷṓws (acc. pl.)
idioms.how: h₂éǵeti with gʷṓws as OBJ in the plural; bʰérdʰt 'plunder, capture' for raiding people or goods
idioms.source: West 2007 ch. 12 'Cattle raids' (Ved. gáviṣṭi- 'desire for cows' = battle, OIr. Táin Bó); M&A 2006 §17.5 (OIr. táin 'raid' < *to-ag-no-)

idioms.idiom: drive off (h₂éǵeti) or snatch (h₁r̥h₁pyéti) the captives (kaptós)
idioms.how: kaptós is an adjective: as a noun it needs a gender ('the captives' = kaptós, gender m or f, PL)
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §17.2 (Lat. rapiō 'carry off, plunder'), §17.5 (*kaptos 'captive')

idioms.idiom: pay the kʷoynéh₂ (kʷinéwti + kʷoynéh₂)
idioms.how: 'he ransomed his son' = 'he paid the price for his son'
idioms.source: Beekes 2010 s.v. ποινή 'ransom, fine, penalty, vengeance' (Il.); M&A 2006 §17.4 (Gk tínō 'make someone pay a debt, ransom, fine')

idioms.idiom: kʷéyeti in the middle 'exact payment for oneself'; the blood-price is kʷoynéh₂
idioms.how: kʷéyeti, voice MID, OBJ the wrongdoer; a feud is 'the kʷoynéh₂ between the clans'
idioms.source: LIV² 3.*kʷei̯- (Ved. cáyate 'punishes'; Gk τίνομαι 'avenge'); Beekes s.v. ποινή

idioms.idiom: gʷṓws with the slot gender f
idioms.how: gʷṓws is of common gender and masculine in the engine; a cow as a female animal takes "gender": "f" on its slot and on its pronouns: 'the white cow' = albʰéh₂ gʷṓws, 'his cows' = swā́s gʷṓs, 'them' = tā́s or h₁íh₂n̥s. Cattle in general can stay masculine. For a bull or an ox see 'bull, ox'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §9.2 *gʷṓus 'cow'; EWAia I s.v. gáv- m. f. 'cattle, bull, cow'; Beekes 2010 s.v. βοῦς [f., m.] 'cow, bull, ox'; rounds 3 and 5

idioms.idiom: wetsós 'yearling' as a noun
idioms.how: wetsós is an adjective: give the slot a gender (m)
idioms.source: EWAia s.v. vatsá- 'calf'; round 3

idioms.idiom: 'the young one': h₂yuHn̥ḱós with gender f; or dʰugh₂tḗr 'daughter'
idioms.how: h₂yuHn̥ḱós in a noun role with "gender": "f"
idioms.source: M&A 2006 ch. 12 reconstructs no 'girl'; round 3 judgement: 'the young one' (h₂yuHn̥ḱós, f.) or 'daughter'

idioms.idiom: lead home the bride: wédʰeti + snusós
idioms.how: 'he married her' = 'he led her (home)' (wédʰeti, OBJ the woman); the bride is snusós; the bride-price h₁wédmn̥
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §12.2 *h₂wedʰ- 'lead in marriage' (Lith. vedù 'lead, marry', W dyweddïo, Skt vadhū́- 'bride'), §12.3 *snusós (Gk νυός, Ru. snokhá 'son's wife; bride')

idioms.idiom: woyḱós 'settler, fellow villager'
idioms.how: the man of the same settlement (ḱóymos); Skt prátiveśa- 'neighbour' is práti + veśá-
idioms.source: EWAia s.v. veśá-; round 3

idioms.idiom: 'be of one mind': a nominal clause with the bahuvrihi sm̥ + ménos
idioms.how: PRED = compound {first: closed:prefix/sm, second: pie-lex-menos, type: bahuvrihi}: 'we agree' = 'we (are) of one mind'
idioms.source: the compound 'of one mind' (Gk ὁμόφρων) from *sm̥- 'one' + 'mind'; round 3

idioms.idiom: 'not want': ne + wéḱti or wélh₁ti
idioms.how: neg: "ne" on wéḱti/wélh₁ti; for a refused gift say 'he did not take it'
idioms.source: LIV² *h₂res- 'sich verweigern' has no usable lexeme (Av. rārəšiieiṇti, Gk ἀρνέομαι, different formations)

idioms.idiom: solh₂wós 'whole, all' as a noun
idioms.how: solh₂wós has a NOUN spec: it cannot be a MOD. Use it as its own slot with a gender ('all (of them) came' = solh₂wós, gender m, PL). For 'each', repeat the noun or say 'one by one'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §11.7 *sólwos 'whole' (Skt sárva- 'all'); Fortson §7.27 (Lat. quisque 'each' is kʷis + -kʷe, not in the engine)

idioms.idiom: h₁óynos 'one, single' or somHós 'alone'
idioms.how: 'only the shepherd' = 'the shepherd alone' (somHós as MOD)
idioms.source: de Vaan 2008 s.v. ūnus (Lat. ūnicus 'sole'); round 3

idioms.idiom: éti
idioms.how: an ADV slot
idioms.source: de Vaan 2008 s.v. et (PIE *h₁eti 'still, also'; Gk ἔτι)

idioms.idiom: de (contrastive) or h₂éti
idioms.how: de after the first word of the contrasting clause
idioms.source: Fortson 2010 §7.28 (*de, Gk δέ); de Vaan s.v. at (Lat. at 'but' < *h₂eti)

idioms.idiom: h₂éti 'back, again' as an ADV before the verb
idioms.how: 'give back' = h₂éti déh₃t; 'repay' = gʰéldʰeti
idioms.source: de Vaan 2008 s.v. at (OIr. aith- 'again', Lith. at- 'back')

idioms.idiom: 'not X, but Y'
idioms.how: two clauses: neg on the first, de on the second
idioms.source: Gk ἀντί + gen. 'instead of' needs an adposition with a genitive object, which the engine does not take

idioms.idiom: 'before' (préy) or two clauses joined by nu 'then'
idioms.how: 'wait until he comes' = 'wait; then he will come'
idioms.source: no PIE 'until' reconstructs (Lat. dum, Gk ἕως, Ved. yā́vat are separate formations)

idioms.idiom: 'for a lifetime': h₂óyu in the accusative of extent
idioms.how: h₂óyu in a GOAL slot (ACC); for 'never' add neg
idioms.source: no PIE 'always' reconstructs; the daughters build it on the 'lifetime' noun (Gk αἰεί beside αἰών, Lat. aevum). Round 3 judgement: the handbooks read here give no reconstructed adverb

idioms.idiom: moḱs 'quickly, early'
idioms.how: an ADV slot
idioms.source: no PIE 'soon'; moḱs is glossed 'quickly; early' (round 3)

idioms.idiom: a perfect or aorist with nu 'now'
idioms.how: 'he has already come' = nu + perfect/aorist
idioms.source: no PIE 'already' reconstructs

idioms.idiom: somHós 'same, alike'
idioms.how: 'he is like his father' = 'he (is) alike to his father' (nominal clause, IO the father); for similes, two clauses
idioms.source: the Vedic simile particles (iva, ná) are not in the engine

idioms.idiom: hunger (gʷoldʰós); 'die of hunger' = mért + INS gʷoldʰós
idioms.how: a famine is 'the hunger' that lies on the land; 'they starved' = 'they died of hunger'
idioms.source: Derksen 2008 s.v. *gȏldъ 'hunger'; LIV² ?*su̯eld- 'starve' is Germanic only

idioms.idiom: 'die in the water': mért + LOC wódr̥
idioms.how: LOC slot wódr̥
idioms.source: no PIE 'drown' (PGmc *kwabjan- 'choke' is Germanic only)

idioms.idiom: 'lay in the earth': dʰéǵʰōm in the locative
idioms.how: stĺ̥neh₂ 'pillar, gravestone' for a marker
idioms.source: no PIE word for 'grave' (Gmc *hlaiwa-, Gk θήκη, Slavic *grobъ are branch words)

idioms.idiom: néḱus or mr̥tós as a noun ('the dead one')
idioms.how: an adjective with a gender in a noun role; plural for 'the dead'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §11.7 (*néḱus: Gk νέκυς 'corpse', Av. nasu- 'corpse')

idioms.idiom: wish evil: wéḱti + h₂egʰós (Tier 3: no inherited verb)
idioms.how: 'he cursed them' = 'he wished them evil' (optative of a harm verb also works)
idioms.source: LIV² *ḱep- '(ver)fluchen' is Vedic only (śápati); the coinage ḱépeti is Tier 3b

idioms.idiom: name the weapon: ǵʰoysós 'spear, missile', gʷéru 'spear', ḱéstrom 'knife, blade'
idioms.how: a sword is ḱéstrom (Skt śástra- 'knife, sword'); an arrow is ǵʰoysós 'missile'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §15.4: no PIE 'weapon' or 'sword' (*wēben is Germanic-Tocharian)

idioms.idiom: h₂éyos 'metal, copper, bronze'
idioms.how: iron is post-PIE: say 'metal'

idioms.idiom: 'the proclaiming man': wiHrós with ḱénst as a participle
idioms.how: wiHrós with a MOD slot ḱénst, "participle": {"voice": "ACT"}: ḱn̥sónts wiHrós; or a relative clause 'who proclaims'
idioms.source: No PIE 'herald': M&A 2006 §21.1–21.2 (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/030_part0029.txt) gives Gk κῆρυξ beside Skt kārú- 'poet' (*kāru-, its IE status challenged) and Gk καλήτωρ 'herald' from 'call' (Greek only); round 5

idioms.idiom: give (déh₃t) and repay (gʰéldʰeti); the debt is dʰl̥gʰós
idioms.how: 'lend' = 'give, and he will repay'; 'borrow' = 'take (h₁épt) and owe (dʰl̥gʰéti)'
idioms.source: no PIE 'lend' (Go. leihvan, from *lei̯kʷ- 'leave', is Germanic; NIL loykʷéh₂ is single-branch)

idioms.idiom: 'to him there is much wealth' / 'to him there is no wealth': the dative of possession with h₃épnos
idioms.how: the owner in an IO slot (dative), h₃épnos SUBJ with polh₁ús as its MOD, V h₁ésti: 'the man is rich' = polh₁ú h₃épnos wiHrṓy h₁ésti; 'the man is poor' = the same with "neg": true and no polh₁ús (h₃épnos wiHrṓy ne h₁ésti), or h₁égos 'lack'. As an attribute ('a rich man'): a POSS 'a man of much wealth'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §17.3 (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/026_part0025.txt): no PIE 'rich'; the daughters derive it from the 'wealth' word (Lat. opulentus, Hitt. happina(nt)-, Av. afnahvant-; EWAia s.v. ápnas-: Ved. ápnasvant-, YAv. afnaŋhant- 'rich in goods', Hitt. happinant-; raw/books/text/ewaia-v1/p0143.txt) or *h₁su-dʰh₁-énos (Greek–Indic, not in the lexicon); Lat. pauper is from *pau- 'little' (West Central only). The mihi est possessive: Handbook vol. 3, 'Proto-Indo-European' ch. §8 (Latin, Greek, Vedic, Tocharian; raw/books/text/handbook-klein-v3/055_14_chapter08_10.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: the heir (h₃órbʰos) takes the father's wealth
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §12.2 (*h₂/₃orbʰos 'orphan, heir')

idioms.idiom: dʰoHnéh₂ 'grain (prepared as food)'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §16.1; round 2 (no PIE 'bread')

idioms.idiom: dóru 'tree' in the plural
idioms.source: round 2: h₁widʰh₁us has no accent

idioms.idiom: h₂ówis 'sheep' (feminine)
idioms.source: h₂ówis is f.; *h₃ēwis (Gmc *awiz) has no usable entry

idioms.idiom: gʰréh₁mn̥ 'grass'
idioms.how: 'dry grass'
idioms.source: Balto-Slavic *sḗnа 'hay' and Lat. fēnum have no usable entry

idioms.idiom: h₁éwseti 'burn (something)' + dṓm
idioms.source: round 3

idioms.idiom: léykʷt 'leave (behind)'
idioms.how: an exposed child is 'left' (on the hill)
idioms.source: LIV² *lei̯kʷ-

idioms.idiom: HréwdHti 'weep, wail, lament'
idioms.source: LIV² *reu̯dH-

idioms.idiom: 'the hunting man': wiHrós with wrégeti as a participle
idioms.how: wiHrós with a MOD slot wrégeti, "participle": {"voice": "ACT"}: wrégonts wiHrós 'the hunter', pl. wrégontes wiHrṓs; or a relative clause 'who hunts'
idioms.source: No PIE agent noun of the hunt (round 3); h₂éǵreh₂ 'catch, hunt' and h₂eǵro- are NIL single-branch / unusable; round 5

idioms.idiom: the storm god's work: Perkʷunos strikes; thunder is gʰrómos
idioms.how: 'lightning struck' = pérkʷunos + a strike verb; 'it thundered' = gʰrómos as SUBJ or OBJ ('we heard the thunder')
idioms.source: *meldʰn- 'lightning' has no engine shape: the branches build different stems (Balto-Slavic *mildnis i-stem, Gmc *meldunjaz, OPr. mealde); gʰrómos 'roar, rumble; thunder' (9 reflex groups, offered); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'tired' (ḱeḱómh₂e) or 'not working'
idioms.source: l̥h₁dós (Gmc *lata-) has a noun spec only

idioms.idiom: no usable inherited word: describe it
idioms.how: cloak = wésmn̥ 'garment'; bucket = kʷéros 'pot'; bee = 'the honey-maker' (médʰu)
idioms.source: round 3 (spindle and deer have their own entries since round 5): entries unaccented, unusable or single-branch (see the audit); M&A 2006 §9.5 *bʰikʷó- 'bee' (OIr. bech, NE bee, OCS bьčela) is North-Western and has no entry

idioms.idiom: uksḗn 'bull, ox', or gʷṓws with the slot gender m
idioms.how: uksḗn (m.) names the bull or draught ox; or gʷṓws, masculine in the engine ('the great bull' = méǵh₂s gʷṓws; "gender": "m" on the slot makes it explicit)
idioms.source: EWAia I s.v. gáv- (m. 'bull', f. 'cow'); Beekes 2010 s.v. βοῦς (m. 'ox, bull'); M&A 2006 §9.2 *uk(ʷ)sēn- 'ox', the male as against the three 'cow' words (NWels ych, NE ox, Skt ukṣán-, Toch. B okso); round 5

idioms.idiom: the plural in the oblique cases: 'with (both) hands' = ǵʰesr̥bʰís
idioms.how: the dual exists only in the nominative, vocative and accusative; an oblique (INS, DAT, GEN, ABL, LOC) of two things takes the plural with no numeral: 'he held it with two hands' = ǵʰésōr as INS with "num": "PL" (ǵʰesr̥bʰís), not "DU" (which silently falls back to the plural) and not a dwóh₁ MOD (check_plan rejects 'two' in an oblique case). This is also the way for two cows (feminine) in an oblique case. To count them, put the two in a nominative or accusative clause: 'he has two hands' (dwóh₁ ǵʰésore), 'he took two cows'
idioms.source: Fortson 2010 §6.13: the dual cases other than nom./voc./acc. cannot be reconstructed, the daughters differ too much (raw/books/text/fortson/016_9781405188968_006.txt); Ringe 2006 p. 47 leaves the oblique dual out of its paradigms for the same reason (raw/books/text/ringe/p0058.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: no infinitive: a dative verbal noun ('for crossing') where the lexicon offers one, else an imperative clause plus the verb in the subjunctive
idioms.how: (1) a -tu- action noun of the verb in an IO (dative) slot: 'teach me to cross' = ḱéHst AOR IMP 2SG + me (OBJ, enclitic) + pértus as IO: pr̥téwey me ḱHsdʰí (offered: pértus 'crossing', gʷémtus 'coming', ǵéwstus 'tasting', stéh₂tus 'standing'). (2) Otherwise two clauses: the imperative of ḱéHst with OBJ me, then the verb in the 1st-person subjunctive ('teach me: I shall swim'): ḱHsdʰí me. snéh₂oh₂. 'learn to X' = h₁éwkt 'become used to' with the verbal noun, or the verb on its own
idioms.source: Fortson 2010 §5.58: the daughters' infinitives are frozen case forms of verbal nouns, and which of them are PIE is uncertain; the dative of -tu- nouns is one (Ved. pā́tave 'for drinking'), raw/books/text/fortson/015_9781405188968_005.txt; round 5

idioms.idiom: gʰréh₁mn̥ 'grass, green growth'; a healing herb is gʰréh₁mn̥ with the active participle of mḗdeti
idioms.how: OBJ/SUBJ gʰréh₁mn̥ (n.); for 'healing herb' add a MOD slot pie-lex-mexdeti with "participle": {"voice": "ACT"} and head = the noun: wiHrós mḗdont gʰréh₁mn̥ déh₃t
idioms.source: No PIE word for 'herb' or 'plant' (M&A 2006 §10.2: no PIE 'grass' either); de Vaan 2008 s.v. grāmen (raw/books/text/devaan-latin/p0283.txt) gives only 'grass', so the gloss is not widened; M&A 2006 §11.7 *med- 'heal, cure' (Lat. medeor, Av. vī-mad- 'healer'; raw/books/text/mallory-adams/020_part0019.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'what heals': the verb mḗdeti, or gʰréh₁mn̥ 'herb' with its participle
idioms.how: say 'heal' with the verb (mḗdeti, OBJ the sick person); a medicine as a thing = gʰréh₁mn̥ + MOD participle of mḗdeti (ACT), 'the healing herb'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §11.7: two PIE 'healing' roots, *h₁eis- and *med- (Lat. medeor, medicus 'doctor', Av. vī-mad- 'healer'); no noun 'medicine' reconstructs (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/020_part0019.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: no usable 'hair' word: use the specific word (beard, mane, wool/fleece) or describe the head
idioms.how: beard = bʰardʰéh₂; a horse's mane = gʷriHwéh₂; animal hair, fleece = h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ 'wool'; 'curly-haired' = kripsós (adj.); otherwise rephrase without 'hair'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §11.2 lists many hair words (*ḱripo- 'head hair', *pou-m-s- 'body hair', *pilos 'a single hair', *dʰrigʰ-), none in the lexicon with a usable accented entry (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/020_part0019.txt); gowros 'lock of hair' (Balto-Slavic, Norw.) has no accent; round 5

idioms.idiom: no usable 'staff' word: h₃ósdos 'branch, bough'
idioms.how: a staff or stick = h₃ósdos 'branch' (a cut bough); 'he leans on a staff' → 'he walks with a branch' (INS h₃ósdoh₁)
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §13.2 *ǵʰasdʰos 'rod, staff' (Lat. hasta, OE gierd) and §15 *bak- 'staff' (OIr. bacc, Lat. baculum, Gk βάκτρον) have no usable lexicon entry (bakos, bakkos, baktlo-: unaccented, single-branch stems) (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/022_part0021.txt, 024_part0023.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the fathers': ph₂tḗr in the plural; one begetter = ǵénh₁tōr
idioms.how: the ancestors = ph₂tḗr with "num": "PL" ('to join the fathers' = GOAL ph₂térn̥s); a founding ancestor, 'begetter' = ǵénh₁tōr
idioms.source: West 2007 ch. 10 'Going to join the fathers': the dead of one's family are 'the fathers' in Indic and other traditions (Ved. pitáraḥ) (raw/books/text/west/017_ch10.txt); M&A 2006 §12 *ǵénh₁tōr 'begetter, procreator' (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/021_part0020.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: no noun 'wound' in the lexicon: say it with the verb térh₃t or h₃wáth₂t 'wound'
idioms.how: 'his wound is deep' → 'he was badly wounded' (térh₃t, aorist; the wounded man OBJ); 'they tended his wound' → mḗdeti 'they healed him'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §11.7: *wol/r-no/eh₂- 'wound' (Lat. volnus, Alb. varrë, Rus. rána, Skt vraṇá-) in different grades and stems, and the Baltic-Greek *weh₂t- (Lith. votìs, Gk ὠτειλή); neither has a lexicon entry or one formation in two branches (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/020_part0019.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'heat' (tépos) or 'burning' (h₁éwseti) of the sick
idioms.how: 'he has a fever' = 'heat burns him' (SUBJ tépos, OBJ the sick man, V h₁éwseti) or 'he burns' (h₁éwseti MID)
idioms.source: the daughters name fever 'heat, burning': Hitt. tapašša- 'fever, heat' from *tep- (M&A 2006 §20.9, raw/books/text/mallory-adams/029_part0028.txt); Alb. ethe 'fever' from *h₁ews- 'burn' (M&A 2006 §8.2, raw/books/text/mallory-adams/017_part0016.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the knowing one': ǵn̥h₃rós as a noun, with widét 'see' for what he foresees
idioms.how: ǵn̥h₃rós is an adjective: give the slot a gender (m), or MOD of wiHrós ('the knowing man'); 'he sees what will come' with widét
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §20.2 *wet- 'see (truly)': Lat. vātēs 'seer', OIr. fáith 'prophet' (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/029_part0028.txt); the lexicon's weh₂tis (Lat. vātēs, PCelt. *wātis) is unaccented with no usable spec, and wéh₂tus (PCelt. *wātus, PGmc *wōþuz) is unglossed. M&A §23.2: priest/seer *kowh₁ēys (Gk κοίης, Lyd. kaweś, Skt kaví-) is insecure and not in the lexicon (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/032_part0031.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: no PIE 'priest': 'the man who pours (offerings) to the gods'
idioms.how: a relative clause on wiHrós: h₁yós deywóybʰos ǵʰéwt 'who poured to the gods' (ǵʰéwt, aorist; IO deywós PL); or name his act with the verb
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §23.2: the PIE words for 'priest' are insecure (*kowh₁ēys, Lat. flāmen ~ Skt brahmán-) (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/032_part0031.txt); §22.11: Skt hótar- 'priest' is 'the one who pours' (juhóti) from *ǵʰew- (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/031_part0030.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'be well-minded': the bahuvrihi h₁su + ménos (Gk εὐμενής, Skt sumánas-)
idioms.how: PRED = compound {first: closed:prefix/h1su, second: pie-lex-menos, type: bahuvrihi} with a gender; 'have mercy on me' = IMP h₁ésti 2SG + IO 'me' + PRED: déywe méǵʰye h₁suménēs h₁sdʰí; 'spare him' can also be 'do not kill him' (neg mē + IMP)
idioms.source: the lexicon's h₁sumenēs 'well-disposed' (Gk εὐμενής, Myc., Skt sumánas-; unusable as a lexeme, built here by the compound engine); M&A 2006 has no PIE 'mercy' or 'pity'; round 5

idioms.idiom: no usable 'shame' word: name the fear or the bad name
idioms.how: 'I am ashamed' → 'I fear (what men will say)'; 'it is a shame' → 'it is bad' (an adjective PRED); pick the words with lexq (fear, bad, name)
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §17.4: *h₂eygʷʰes- 'shame' is West Central (Goth. aiwiski, Gk αἶσχος), and *h₂eh₂gos 'guilt' Greek-Indic (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/026_part0025.txt); Kroonen 2013 s.v. *aiwiskja- (raw/books/text/kroonen-pgmc/p0025.txt) derives Goth. aiwiski from *h₂eigʷʰ-isk-, a different formation from the Greek s-stem, so no single formation in two branches; no lexicon entry; round 5

idioms.idiom: 'point out the right': déyḱeti (or the aorist dḗyḱst) with h₃reǵtós in the neuter
idioms.how: OBJ h₃reǵtós with "gender": "n" ('the right'), V déyḱeti: h₃reǵtóm déyḱeti 'he judges'; a judge = wiHrós + relative clause 'who shows the right'
idioms.source: Lat. iūdex 'judge' < *ieuos-dik- 'who shows the law' (de Vaan 2008 s.v. iūs p. 316, raw/books/text/devaan-latin/p0330.txt); Gk δίκη 'judgement, right' to *deyḱ- 'show'; M&A 2006 §17.4 *yew(e)s- 'law, ritual norm' (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/026_part0025.txt) has no lexicon entry, so h₃reǵtós 'straight, right' stands for the right; round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the man who saw': a relative clause with widét
idioms.how: wiHrós + h₁yós … widét 'who saw (it)'; 'he bears witness' = 'he says what he saw' (mléwHti + relative clause)
idioms.source: Gk ἵστωρ 'witness, one who knows' is an agent noun of *weyd- 'see, know'; Hitt. kutruwa- 'witness' is 'the fourth (party)' (M&A 2006 §19.1, raw/books/text/mallory-adams/028_part0027.txt); the lexicon's widtrés 'viewer, witness' has no reflexes and no usable spec; the engine has no perfect participle ('having seen'); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'follow, attend on' (sékʷetor, middle) or 'be the servant' (h₃órbʰos)
idioms.how: 'he serves the king' = OBJ the king + V sékʷetor (MID, deponent): wiHrós h₃réǵm̥ sékʷetor; or a nominal clause 'he (is) the king's servant' (PRED h₃órbʰos + POSS)
idioms.source: Gk ἕπομαι 'follow, attend', Ved. sácate 'accompanies' (the entry's reflexes; LIV² *sekʷ-); M&A 2006 §22: *sep- 'touch, serve' (Gk ἕπω, Skt sápati) has only sepelyéti 'to honor' (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/031_part0030.txt); h₃órbʰos 'servant' (round 3); round 5

idioms.idiom: no PIE 'mean': ask what the word says, or what it is
idioms.how: 'What does this word mean?' → 'What does this word say?' (kʷíd OBJ, SUBJ wékʷos, V mléwHti) or 'What (is) this?' (nominal clause); 'I mean …' → 'I say …'
idioms.source: no reconstructed verb 'mean, signify' (M&A 2006 ch. 21 Speech lists none, raw/books/text/mallory-adams/030_part0029.txt); round 5

idioms.idiom: h₂éḱmō 'stone' (the hammer-stone)
idioms.how: name the stone: 'he strikes with the stone' = h₂ḱm̥néh₁ (INS of h₂éḱmō) + the verb; a smith's hammer and anvil are both h₂éḱmō
idioms.source: Kroonen 2013 s.v. *hamara- 'hammer' (ON hamarr 'hammer; crag', OE hamor), related to *h₂eḱ-mon- 'stone, anvil, meteorite' (formal problems with the suffix); Gk ἄκμων 'anvil' (Beekes 2010). No PIE 'hammer' word: Ved. vájra-/Av. vazra- 'cudgel' is Indo-Iranian (M&A 2006 §15); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the sharp bone that sews': h₃ésth₁ + h₂eḱrós with siHwyéti
idioms.how: say what it does: 'she sews with a sharp bone' = h₂eḱróh₁ h₃sth₁éh₁ (INS) siHwyéti; there is no needle noun to use
idioms.source: Lat. acus 'needle' is a u-stem of *h₂eḱ- 'sharp' (Latin only in that sense; pie-lex-h2ekju unusable); M&A 2006 §9 (plants) *skʷēis '±needle and/or thorn' (OIr. scé 'hawthorn', Lith. skujà 'fir-needle': plant needles; pie-lex-skwoyeh2_x_skuyeh2 unusable); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the wood she spins with': dóru (INS) + snéh₁ti
idioms.how: describe the act: 'she spins with the wood' = drúh₁ (INS of dóru) snéh₁ti; replaces 'spindle' in the shared 'describe it' entry
idioms.source: no PIE 'spindle': snéh₁trom (Gk) is not verified (round 3); M&A 2006 §14.2 names spinning but no spindle word; snéh₁ti 'spin' (LIV² *sneh₁-, round 3); round 5

idioms.idiom: sh₂éymn̥ 'rope, strap'
idioms.how: the horse's 'rope': OBJ sh₂éymn̥ with h₁éḱwos in the GEN ('the horse's strap'); sh₂imṓ 'cord, binding' as a second choice
idioms.source: *sh₂ey- 'bind': Gk ἱμάς 'leather strap, thong', ἱμονιά 'rope', OIr. sín 'chain' (the entry's reflexes); M&A 2006 §15.8 *h₂ensiyo/eh₂- 'reins' (Gk ἡνία, OIr. éis(s)i) has no lexicon entry; round 5

idioms.idiom: pinéḱti 'mark with colour, paint, adorn'
idioms.how: 'she dyes the wool red' = 'she colours the wool red': OBJ + pinéḱti, with h₁rudʰrós as a PRED/MOD for the colour
idioms.source: LIV² *pei̯ḱ- (Ved. piṃśáti 'adorns', Lat. pingō 'paint, embroider', OCS pьsati 'write'); M&A 2006 §14.1-2: the dyeing verb *reg- (Gk ῥέζω 'dye', Skt rajyati 'is coloured') is a Graeco-Aryan regional word with no lexicon entry; round 5

idioms.idiom: give to the gods (déh₃t + IO), pour (ǵʰéwt) a libation, or h₁yáǵeti 'worship with sacrifice'
idioms.how: 'we offer mead to the gods' = déywoybʰos médʰu déh₃mes (IO déywos PL); a libation = ǵʰéwt with the liquid as OBJ; the rite itself = h₁yáǵeti with the god as OBJ; 'the sacrifice' (noun) = némos
idioms.source: West 2007 ch. 3-4 (offerings and libations; Ved. juhóti, Gk χέω); LIV² *Hi̯aǵ- p. 224; round 3 ǵʰéwt 'pour'; round 5

idioms.idiom: 'thick milk': h₂mélǵos + bʰénǵʰus (or súHros 'sour')
idioms.how: h₂mélǵos with the MOD bʰénǵʰus 'thick' (neuter); 'sour milk' with súHros
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §16.3: *dʰédʰh₁i 'sour, coagulated milk' (Alb. djathë 'cheese', Skt dádhi, OPr. dadan 'milk') and *twóh₂ 'curdled milk' (Gk τυρός 'cheese'); dʰédʰh₁i is a heteroclitic i/n-stem (Skt gen. dadhnás) with no engine shape, *twóh₂ has no entry; round 5

idioms.idiom: méǵh₂s dṓm 'the great house'
idioms.how: dṓm with the MOD méǵh₂s; 'the king's hall' = h₃rēǵós dṓm (POSS); sédos 'seat, dwelling' for the seat of a chief
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §13.1: NE hall is a Germanic derivative (from *ḱel- 'cover, protect'; Lat. cella 'storeroom'); no PIE 'hall'. dṓm 'house' (9 reflex groups); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'pile up the wood and burn the dead': kʷéyt + dóru, then h₁éwseti / dʰégʷʰeti
idioms.how: two clauses: 'they piled up wood' (OBJ dóru PL, kʷéyt AOR), 'they burned the dead man' (OBJ néḱus, h₁éwseti); 'on the fire' = LOC péh₂wr̥
idioms.source: West 2007 ch. 12 (the hero is cremated on a pyre after a chief orders wood gathered: Il. 23, Rm., Beowulf); LIV² *kʷei̯- 'aufschichten' (printed p. 378) whose Indic nouns cití-, citā́ name the (funeral) pile; round 5

idioms.idiom: the fire burns: péh₂wr̥ / h₁n̥gʷnís + dʰégʷʰeti
idioms.how: 'the flames rose' = 'the fire burned high'; the deified fire h₁n̥gʷnís in address and praise
idioms.source: bʰl̥gmeh₂ 'flame' (Lat. flamma f. < *flag-mā, Gk φλογμός m.: two formations) has no accent, so it is not offered; M&A 2006 §20.3 (*bʰleg- 'burn'). h₂weksíh₂ 'flame' is NIL single-branch; round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the black bird': kr̥snós h₂éwis
idioms.how: h₂éwis with the MOD kr̥snós; a raven on the battlefield = kr̥snós h₂éwis eating the dead (néḱus)
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §9.3: 'crow' *kVr-C- (Lat. corvus, Gk κόραξ; onomatopoeic, vowel unclear) and *wer- (Lith. várna, Ru. voróna, Toch. B wrauña); worno- 'black bird; raven, crow' (Balto-Slavic, Celtic *branos) has no engine shape; round 5

idioms.idiom: 'the bird of the night': h₂éwis + nókʷts (GEN)
idioms.how: h₂éwis with POSS nókʷts ('of the night')
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §9.3, §21.4: owl names are onomatopoeic and regional (*h₂/₃uh₁e/olo- NE owl, Hitt. huwalas; *ul- Lat. ulucus, Skt ulūka-; *ku- OHG hūwo); none has a lexicon entry; round 5

idioms.idiom: h₁ólḱis 'elk', the large deer
idioms.how: a stag or deer in the forest = h₁ólḱis (gender f in the engine; a stag takes slot gender m); replaces 'deer', 'stag' in the shared 'describe it' entry
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §9.1: *h₁élh₁ēn 'deer' (Arm. ełn, Lith. élnis, OCS jelenь; Gk ἔλαφος another formation) is an n-stem the engine cannot inflect (pie-lex-h1elh1exn, no gloss, no shape); *h₁ólḱis 'elk' from the same root (Kroonen s.v. *algi-, Derksen s.v. *olsь) is offered; round 5

idioms.idiom: a manner adverb is the neuter accusative of the adjective: h₁wésu 'well' (h₁wésus 'good'), gʷr̥dú 'slowly' (gʷr̥dús 'slow'), HeHḱú 'swiftly'
idioms.how: the adjective in a GOAL slot with "gender": "n" (the engine has no adverb role for adjectives; GOAL gives the accusative), before the verb: 'he speaks well' = h₁wésu mléwHti; 'speak well!' = h₁wésu mluHdʰí; 'the cattle go home slowly' = dṓm gʷr̥dú h₁yénti. It works beside an OBJ ('he speaks the word well' = wékʷos h₁wésu mléwHti). 'Quickly' can also be moḱs (ADV)
idioms.source: Fortson 2010 §7.23 (PIE had no adverb-forming suffix; case forms of adjectives served, e.g. neuter *méǵh₂ 'greatly': Hitt. mēk, Ved. máhi, Gk μέγα); Handbook (Klein, Joseph & Fritz 2017) vol. 3, 'Proto-Indo-European' ch. §2.3.2 (manner adverbs: the INS of an abstract noun or the neuter ACC of an adjective, Ved. dravát); Gk εὖ 'well' beside εὐ- (Fortson §6.86 *h₁esu- 'good', prefix *h₁su-); round 5

idioms.idiom: orientation facing the sunrise: east = h₂éwsteros 'toward the dawn'; west = wékʷsperos 'evening' (behind); north = sewyós 'left'; south = deḱsiwós 'right'
idioms.how: 'to the west' = wékʷsperos in a GOAL slot ('we go west' = wékʷsperom h₁imés); 'in the west' = LOC. 'North'/'south' = sewyós/deḱsiwós as a noun (GOAL or LOC slot with "gender": "n": 'they go north' = sewyóm h₁yénti), or as a MOD 'the left/right side'. 'East' = h₂éwsteros (LOC with gender n: h₂éwsteroy h₁éyti 'he lives in the east'; MOD 'the eastern sea'). The English stays 'west/north'
idioms.source: M&A 2006 §18.3 and §18.7 (raw/books/text/mallory-adams/027_part0026.txt): only 'east' (*h₂ews-t(e)ro-) reconstructs as a cardinal direction; the system of facing the rising sun (east = front, west = behind, north = left, south = right) reconstructs, but each branch made its own words (OIr. dess, Skt dákṣiṇa- 'right, south'; OIr. fochla 'north' from clé 'left'; Gmc 'north' ~ Umbr. nertru 'left'); 'west' is named from the evening in Germanic (from the root of *wékʷsperos: Lat. vesper, Gk ἕσπερος); round 5

idioms.idiom: 'another land': h₂élyos as the MOD of dʰéǵʰōm; the foreigner is 'the man of another land' or gʰóstis 'stranger, guest'
idioms.how: dʰéǵʰōm with h₂élyos as its MOD: 'in a foreign land, abroad' = LOC (h₂élyeh₂i dʰǵʰémi); 'to a foreign land' = GOAL (h₂élyeh₂m dʰéǵʰōm); 'a foreigner' = wiHrós with a POSS dʰéǵʰōm + MOD h₂élyos (h₂élyeh₂s dʰǵʰmés wiHrós), or gʰóstis
idioms.source: Beekes 2010 s.v. ἀλλοδαπός 'from another land, foreign' (Il.), derived from ἄλλος (raw/books/text/beekes-edg/p0060.txt); de Vaan 2008 s.v. alius (derivative aliēnus 'belonging to others'; raw/books/text/devaan-latin/p0048.txt); Kroonen 2013 s.v. *alja- (Go. aljis; raw/books/text/kroonen-pgmc/p0061.txt); OE el-lende 'foreign' is 'other-land' (Germanic, standard: not read on a page this round); M&A 2006 §17.1 *gʰostis 'guest; stranger, enemy' (026_part0025.txt); round 5
